title: Fynaptix · Nuclear & SMR Research
heading: Nuclear Energy Intelligence
subheading: Small modular reactors, uranium & the AI power-demand trade
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. SMR developers are pre-revenue with long regulatory timelines; verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Google signed a 20-year PPA for 890 MW of new capacity from uprates at 11 existing units across six PJM sites in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, with Constellation committing about $4.3B and the first uprate due online in 2028; a separate 15-year, 2,700 MW PJM supply deal brings the total to roughly 3.6 GW. Constellation rose as much as ~14% on the day and closed Oct 9 at $298.07 — contracted cash flow from existing reactors, not new-build risk

The Oct 7 industry price update has the long-term price at $97.00/lb (+$1.50 month on month) and spot at $89.95/lb, which a market note says has broken out of the $85–$87 range held for most of the year; uranium ETFs jumped 4–5.5% on Oct 6 on heavy volume, but URA ($38.90), URNM ($46.50) and NLR ($103.35) all closed Oct 9 roughly where they were a week earlier

kpis.sub: OKLO AT A 52-WEEK LOW; NUSCALE DOWN 49% YTD
kpis.label: Oklo fell ~5% on Oct 7 and 6.1% on Oct 8 to a $33.70 intraday 52-week low with no company-specific catalyst, leaving it ~52% down YTD at a ~$6.45B market cap against $1.2M of quarterly revenue; NuScale closed at $7.20 (52-week low $7.07, -49% YTD) after reporting just $75K of Q2 revenue — the S&P 500 ETF is up ~14% over the same period

TVA's Clinch River BWRX-300 holds the first US construction permit for the design (Sep 29) but has no disclosed cost, start date or financing partner and a 2032 operating target; Google's Oct 6 deal adds capacity by uprating existing reactors from 2028 — the near-term supply is going to incumbent operators, not pre-revenue developers

rows.angle: Largest US nuclear fleet operator (55 GW post-Calpine); direct data-center PPAs with Microsoft, Meta, Walmart, now Amazon
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 9 at $298.07 (+4.6% on the day; market cap ~$105.6B; forward P/E ~24; 52-week range $228.63–$412.70, so still ~28% below the high) after the Oct 6 Google deal — a 20-year, 890 MW uprate PPA across 11 units with ~$4.3B of Constellation investment, plus a separate 15-year, 2,700 MW PJM supply agreement; this follows the Sep 30 Amazon 690 MW Calvert Cliffs PPA, so two hyperscalers have now contracted existing-fleet output; Crane (TMI-1) restart still targeted for 2027

rows.angle: Major Western uranium producer + 49% of Westinghouse
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 9 at $88.06 (market cap ~$38.3B; 52-week range $77.70–$135.24, ~35% below the high) with forward P/E ~61 — richer than last week even as the long-term uranium price reached $97/lb and spot broke out of its $85–$87 range to $89.95; the squeeze is valuation and timing — Q1 realized price was only $65.45/lb vs. $97 term, utilities remain hesitant to sign new term contracts, and the Westinghouse IPO (confidential S-1 reported Jul 31) still has no public filing or pricing date

rows.angle: Nuclear components, naval reactors, advanced reactor work
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 9 at $143.83 (+7.65% on Oct 6; market cap ~$13.2B; forward P/E ~29; 52-week range $131.86–$241.82, ~40% below the high) — up ~5% from ~$137 a week earlier; the Sep 29 Investor Day targets ($5.5–$6.0B 2030 revenue, $1.1–$1.2B adjusted EBITDA, $8.4B backlog) are the anchor, and the question is whether the sector bounce holds or fades

rows.angle: Grid equipment + BWRX-300 SMR design via GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 9 at $1,004.73 (market cap ~$267.6B; forward P/E ~48; 52-week range $530.16–$1,195.94); the NRC's Sep 29 Clinch River BWRX-300 permit validated the design, but TVA still needs a co-investor and nuclear is a small slice of a company priced on grid and gas-turbine demand; GEV is also held in the Energy Storage sleeve, so avoid double-counting

rows.angle: Fast reactors using recycled waste; Sam Altman-backed; deals directly with AI/data-center customers
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 9 at $34.70 after a 52-week low of $33.70 on Oct 8 (down ~52% YTD; market cap ~$6.45B; 52-week high $193.84); Q2 delivered first revenue ($1.2M, net loss $48.5M), a $1B at-the-market program signed Sep 11 remains a dilution overhang, and the Centrus letter of intent for up to five Aurora powerhouses (deliveries from 2029) still needs a definitive agreement; next catalyst is Q3 results around November

rows.angle: Only SMR design with NRC formal approval; utility-focused; 6 GW TVA/ENTRA1 framework (non-binding)
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 9 at $7.20 (52-week low $7.07; down ~49% YTD; market cap ~$3.1B on ~430M shares) as the $750M at-the-market program filed in August keeps the dilution debate alive; Q2 revenue was only $75K, the TVA PPA (targeted for later this year) is still not binding, and the Clinch River permit went to GE's BWRX-300 rather than NuScale's design — the Oct 6 sector rally (+7%) has not changed that

rows.angle: HALEU enrichment — fuel for advanced reactors
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 9 at $142.44 (market cap ~$2.9B; 52-week range $135.75–$464.25, so within ~5% of the low; down ~41% YTD) after a +8.8% sector-rally day on Oct 6; Q2 revenue rose 14% to $176.1M and backlog is ~$3.0B, but HALEU deliveries for advanced reactors do not start until 2030 and the Oklo letter of intent is not yet a contract

private_watchlist.name: TerraPower
private_watchlist.note: No new Kemmerer milestone this week; the Bechtel split (Sep 21) means the next-phase EPC contract is being rebid, while both sides say the 2030 construction-complete / 2031 commercial-operation schedule is unaffected; the March 2026 Natrium permit remains the only precedent for the Clinch River approval.

private_watchlist.name: X-energy

private_watchlist.name: Helion
private_watchlist.note: No new commercial announcement found this week. The Microsoft PPA (50 MW by 2029 via the Orion plant) stands and OpenAI was previously reported in talks for up to 5GW by 2030; none of it is yet delivered power.

private_watchlist.name: Holtec Nuclear
private_watchlist.note: No new update found this week. The ~$900M Nasdaq listing (HNUC) remains suspended since Sep 16 after a $10.2B valuation target was floated; the S-1 stays on file with no new pricing date.

bear_case.title: Fuel price up, equities not following
bear_case.description: Long-term uranium is $97/lb and spot has broken out to ~$90, yet Oklo is ~52% down YTD, NuScale ~49% and Centrus ~41%, against a ~9% fall for URA and a ~14% rise for the S&P 500 ETF. A one-day sector bounce on Oct 6 (URA +4%, URNM +5%, NLR +5.5%) left the ETFs roughly flat on the week by the Oct 9 close. Counter: Cameco's realized price (Q1 $65.45/lb) still has room to catch up to market.

bear_case.title: A permit is not a reactor
bear_case.description: The Clinch River approval obligates TVA to build nothing: no cost, start date or financing partner has been disclosed and the only timeline is a 2032 operating target. Counter: the NRC finished the review four months early, a genuine improvement in licensing speed.

bear_case.title: Dilution is funding the story
bear_case.description: NuScale has a $750M at-the-market program in place on top of equity issued earlier in 2026, with Q2 revenue of $75K; Oklo carries a $1B program signed Sep 11 against $1.2M of quarterly revenue and has just hit a new 52-week low. Holders are being diluted to pay for commercialization that is years away. Counter: NuScale reports ~$1.9B of liquidity, which removes near-term financing risk.

bear_case.title: Timing mismatch with hyperscaler demand
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers need megawatts in 2027–28, but new SMRs are a 2030s story: both the Google (890 MW, first uprate 2028) and Amazon (190 MW by 2030–32) deals are built on existing reactors and uprates, and went to the incumbent operator. Counter: that is cash flow for Constellation, and contracted demand validates the sector's long-run thesis.
